steps.say: Years of alcohol and smoking scar the pancreas beyond repair. Ducts bead and calcify in a pattern the Cambridge scale grades.
steps.tx: Alcohol and smoking drive most chronic pancreatitis with **TIGAR-O** (risk-factor list) causes, and **Cambridge** (duct-change scale) grades ductal changes from equivocal to marked with **chain-of-lakes** (beaded duct) dilation seen on CT and MRCP in long-standing disease with calcification and atrophy over years.

vis.alt: Comparison of normal pancreas with healthy acini against chronic pancreatitis with fibrosis, calcifications, inflammation and atrophy.
vis.caption: Chronic pancreatitis: fibrosis, calcifications and atrophy replacing healthy tissue. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A widely dilated duct with a small head mass drains well sideways. Sewing a bowel loop along the opened duct relieves pain durably.
steps.tx: Dilated duct over **7 mm** (seven millimetres) with head mass under **4 cm** (four centimetres) suits **Partington-Rochelle** (sideways drainage operation), or **lateral pancreaticojejunostomy** (duct-to-bowel side join), draining the whole duct to relieve pain with lasting relief in most carefully selected patients worldwide.

steps.say: A bulky inflamed head with a normal-calibre duct needs coring out. Beger removes the head while sparing duodenum and bile duct.
steps.tx: **Beger** (head-coring operation), a **duodenum-preserving** (gut-sparing) head resection, cores out the pancreatic head for inflammatory mass with portal hypertension, preserving duodenum and bile duct continuity and suits younger patients needing lifelong exocrine function with lower diabetes risk than Whipple afterwards in reported series.

steps.say: Head mass plus a dilated duct suits a combined approach. Frey cores the head and drains the duct in one operation.
steps.tx: **Frey** (coring plus drainage), combining **head coring** (head excavation) with lateral drainage, treats head mass with dilated duct, giving pain relief matching Whipple with lower morbidity and shorter recovery and preserved gut continuity for better nutrition in experienced pancreatic centres worldwide.

steps.say: Disease hiding between duodenum and pancreas mimics cancer closely. Cysts in the duodenal wall point toward groove pancreatitis.
steps.tx: **Groove pancreatitis** (duodenum-pancreas cleft disease), or **paraduodenal** (beside-duodenum) pancreatitis, shows duodenal wall cysts with Brunner hyperplasia mimicking cancer, and pancreaticoduodenectomy is chosen when malignancy cannot be excluded safely after endoscopic biopsy and full staging scans, with frozen section at operation always.

vis.alt: Anatomical illustration of groove pancreatitis with fibrous tissue, thickened duodenal wall and cysts between pancreatic head and duodenum.
vis.caption: Groove pancreatitis: fibrosis and duodenal wall cysts in the paraduodenal groove. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Inherited pancreatitis strikes young and turns malignant early. Gene carriers need lifelong cancer watch from age forty.
steps.tx: Hereditary **PRSS1** (trypsinogen gene) pancreatitis carries **40 percent** (forty percent) lifetime pancreatic cancer risk with surveillance from age **40** (forty), and total pancreatectomy with **islet autotransplant** (own insulin-cell graft) suits intractable small-duct disease with enzyme replacement and diabetes care after surgery.

steps.say: Milky fluid in the belly or chest after pancreatitis means a duct leak. Amylase over a thousand confirms pancreatic origin.
steps.tx: **Pancreatic ascites** (pancreatic belly fluid) and pleural effusion with amylase over **1000 units per L** (one thousand units) need octreotide with ERCP stenting of the **duct disruption** (duct break), and surgery when leaks persist beyond **3 weeks** (three weeks) despite drainage.

steps.say: A clotted splenic vein raises pressure on the stomach side. Gastric varices then bleed while the rest of the portal system stays normal.
steps.tx: Splenic vein thrombosis with **sinistral portal hypertension** (left-sided high pressure) and gastric varices needs **splenectomy** (spleen removal), while pseudoaneurysm of the splenic artery over **2 cm** (two centimetres) needs embolisation with vaccination cover before and after operation and lifelong bleeding watch.
